Sam: pushed attn-kernel perf patch last night, noticed nightly inference runner OOMs on a few QA traces. rolling back now but wanted to capture notes.
Olga: ugh. which runner / config? dedicated or hosted? :grimacing:
Sam: dedicated gpu pool (dev-dedicated-gpu-3), model=redwood-chat-xl, seq_len=2048, batch=1. OOMs started immediately after kernel change that splits attention workspace differently.
Kevin: did you see fragmentation or a single large alloc fail? quick logs help.
Sam: single large alloc fail. gist of error:

```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.18 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total capacity; 13.62 GiB already allocated; 0 bytes free; 1.18 GiB requested)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ... alloc.cu:234 allocate_chunk
```

Sam: here's truncated torch allocator summary we grabbed before rollback:

```
Allocated tensors: 13.62 GiB
Cached blocks: 1.12 GiB
Active segments: 18
Largest free block: 8.5 MiB
recent_allocations: [64MB, 512MB, 1.2GB(fail)]
expandable_segments: enabled
max_split_size_mb: 64
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.8
```

Zara: that "Largest free block 8.5MiB" screams fragmentation. if kernel now requests contiguous workspace per-layer it will fail even if total free memory looks ok.
Olga: agree. two levers to try: raise max_split_size_mb to allow larger contiguous splits, or enable more aggressive GC (lower garbage_collection_threshold) so cached blocks get freed earlier. also check expandable_segments behavior — it can backfire if it creates many small segments.
Kevin: can you repro locally with the same seq_len/batch? if so run this small script to dump arena state before/after layer 14 where alloc spikes:

```
python repro_alloc_dump.py --model redwood-chat-xl --seq 2048 --layer-watch 14 --dump /tmp/alloc.json
```

Sam: repro is flaky but I reproduced once. attached dump showed many ~1MB fragments and a heap of small segments. The attempted allocation wanted 1.18 GiB contiguous, and allocator tried to split segments but max_split_size_mb prevented merging/splitting effectively.
Zara: my quick config proposals (we tested similar on smaller models):

```
# runtime allocator knobs (example env or config)
{
  "allocator.expandable_segments": "true",
  "allocator.max_split_size_mb": "128",
  "allocator.garbage_collection_threshold": "0.55",
  "allocator.enable_prefix_cache_trimming": "true"
}
```

Zara: raising max_split_size_mb to 128 helped one of our repros in the past by allowing the allocator to coalesce. lowering garbage_collection_threshold to ~0.5 forces earlier trimming of cached blocks.
Olga: also consider a short-term mitigation: for the kernel change, fall back to old workspace layout if contiguous > 512MB is requested. add a guard in kernel-selection: if requested_workspace > limit then use legacy kernel.
Kevin: +1 on guard. For longer-term, we should improve the allocator's split/merge heuristics: prefer merging adjacent free blocks that were created from the same segment and opportunistically move small allocations to a staging pool to reduce fragmentation.
Sam: noted. I rolled patch back but left the branch alive. action items:
- Sam: add guard in scheduler to fallback to legacy kernel for >512MB contiguous workspace (PR by EOD)
- Kevin/Zara: prototype increasing max_split_size_mb and GC threshold tuning on staging (next 48h)
- Olga: file infra experiment to run 24h rerun with knobs and collect torch.cuda.memory_summary() every 5 mins (ticket created: INF-2142)

ci-bot: nightly run for dev-dedicated-gpu-3 failed 3/5 tasks — reverting deployment.
alloc-bot: suggestion: simulate fragmentation by running many small allocations with the same growth pattern to stress reproducible failure.

Sam: short-term patch is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/5823 — adds workspace size guard + telemetry for attempted contiguous allocation sizes. will re-run repro harness and report back.
Olga: thanks. please attach the alloc dumps to the ticket. also add a short test that asserts fallback happens when contiguous workspace>512MB to prevent accidental reverts.
Zara: will run knob matrix: max_split_size_mb=[64,96,128], gc_threshold=[0.45,0.55,0.7] across 3 seeds and post heatmap.
Kevin: if heatmap shows improvement with 96/0.55 that's probably lowest-risk default. try to avoid 128 unless needed for perf.
Sam: good plan. I'll leave the branch open and copy alloc dumps to INF-2142. ping if you want pair debugging.
Zara: :thumbsup:
